extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for petitions, benefit/priority claims, office actions, timing, and extensions in ex parte reexamination proceedings before the USPTO (MPEP §2258–§2265).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to accept unintentionally delayed foreign priority claim (37 CFR 1.55(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: To correct an unintentionally delayed foreign priority claim, file a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.55(e) in the file of the application which matured into the patent to be reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items include: (a) an application data sheet, oath, or declaration (unless previously submitted or exception in 37 CFR 1.55(h) applies); (b) the petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(m); and (c) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional. The Director may require additional information if the unintentionality is in question; petitions filed more than two years after the due date require additional explanation of the circumstances. In the reexamination proceeding, file a separate letter notifying the Office that the petition and attachments are being concurrently filed in the application file. When a decision is rendered in the application file, a copy of the decision and, if granted, the application data sheet (as determined to meet 1.55(e)) will be placed in the reexamination file. See MPEP §214.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoring right of foreign priority when subsequent filing was delayed (37 CFR 1.55(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: To restore foreign priority where the filing of the subsequent application was delayed, file a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.55(c) in the application specified by that rule (not in the reexamination proceeding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: petition and any attachments (including application data sheet) in the specified application file; additionally, file a separate letter in the reexamination proceeding notifying that the petition and attachments are concurrently being filed in the specified application (identifying the application number). When a decision on the petition is rendered in the specified application file, a copy of the decision and, if granted, a copy of the application data sheet determined to meet 1.55(c) will be placed in the reexamination file. See MPEP §213.03, subsection III.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming domestic benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 (applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a patent to be reexamined that matured from an application filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, the patent owner must file in the file of the application which matured into the patent: a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.78(e), required application data, fee, and statement of unintentional delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items: (a) grantable petition for an unintentionally delayed benefit claim (37 CFR 1.78(e)); (b) an application data sheet including the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78(d)(2) (37 CFR 1.76(b)(5)), unless previously submitted; (c) petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(m); (d) a statement that the entire delay between the due date and filing was unintentional (with additional explanation required if >2 years after due date). In the reexamination proceeding, file a separate letter notifying the Office that items (a)-(d) are being concurrently filed in the application file. When a decision under 37 CFR 1.78(e) is rendered in the application file, a copy of the decision and, if granted, the application data sheet determined to meet 1.78(e) will be placed in the reexamination file. See MPEP §211.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming domestic benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 (applications filed before Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For patents that matured from applications filed before Sept 16, 2012, similar petition and filing requirements apply, but the patent owner may either file an application data sheet in the application file or file an amendment in the reexamination inserting the required reference in the first sentence(s) of the specification following the title (per 37 CFR 1.78(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: (a) grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.78(e); (b) unless the patent owner files the amendment in the reexamination, file an application data sheet including the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78(d)(2); (c) petition fee 1.17(m); (d) statement that entire delay was unintentional (with extra explanation if >2 years). If the patent owner chooses to file the amendment in the reexamination, the amendment must insert the required reference in the first sentence(s) of the specification per 1.78(h). In the reexamination, file a letter notifying concurrent filing. When decision is rendered, copies of decision and any application data sheet determined to meet requirements will be placed in the reexamination file. See MPEP §211.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) (provisional) for applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: To correct failure to claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) for a patent matured from a utility or plant application filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, file a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.78(c) in the file of the application which matured into the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: (a) grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.78(c); (b) an application data sheet including the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) and 37 CFR 1.78(a)(3) to the prior provisional application (unless previously submitted); (c) petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(m); (d) a statement that the entire delay between the due date and filing was unintentional (extra explanation required if >2 years). File a separate letter in the reexamination proceeding notifying that these items are being concurrently filed. When decision is rendered in the application file, a copy of the decision and, if granted, the application data sheet determined to meet requirements will be placed in the reexamination file. See MPEP §211.02 and §211.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) (provisional) for applications filed before Sept 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: For patents matured from utility or plant applications filed before Sept 16, 2012, the patent owner must either file the application data sheet in the application file or file an amendment in the reexamination inserting the required provisional reference in the first sentence(s) of the specification per 37 CFR 1.78(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: (a) grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.78(c); (b) unless filing the amendment in the reexamination, an application data sheet including the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) and 37 CFR 1.78(a)(3); (c) petition fee 1.17(m); (d) statement that the delay was unintentional (additional explanation if >2 years). If the patent owner does not choose to file the application data sheet in the application file, an amendment inserting the reference in the first sentence(s) of the specification in the reexamination is acceptable. In the reexamination, file a letter notifying concurrent filing; when decision rendered, copies placed in reexamination file. See MPEP §211.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoring benefit of a provisional application where subsequent filing was delayed (37 CFR 1.78(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To restore the benefit of a provisional application when filing of the subsequent nonprovisional application was unintentionally delayed, file a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.78(b) in the file of the subsequent application which matured into the patent to be reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: grantable petition and any required attachments including an application data sheet meeting 1.78(b) requirements, filed in the subsequent application file. File a separate letter in the reexamination proceeding notifying the Office that the petition and attachments are concurrently filed in the application (identify application number). Design applications cannot claim the benefit of provisional applications. When a decision is rendered in the application file, a copy of the decision and, if granted, the application data sheet determined to meet 1.78(b) will be placed in the reexamination file. See MPEP §211.01(a), subsection II.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Office action completeness and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s first Office action in reexamination must be a complete statement of the examiner's position and sufficiently detailed so the second action can properly be made final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action must clearly set forth the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to each rejected claim. If the request included material such as claim charts, the examiner may incorporate them but must carefully review them to ensure they clearly and completely address patentability. The first action should respond to the substance of each argument raised by the patent owner and requester (37 CFR 1.510, 1.530, 1.535) and treat inappropriate arguments per 37 CFR 1.552(c). If the examiner relies on a patent owner statement (37 CFR 1.501(a)(2)) to interpret claim meaning, the requester must explain how that statement is used. The first action should caution the patent owner that a complete response is necessary because the next action is expected to be final, and that 37 CFR 1.116(b) will be strictly enforced after final action; form paragraph 22.04 is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of dependent claims in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat dependent claims when base claims are rejected, canceled, or no longer subject to reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an unamended base patent claim has been rejected, canceled, or is no longer subject to reexamination, any claim directly or indirectly dependent thereon should be confirmed or allowed if the dependent claim is otherwise allowable. Do not object to or reject a dependent claim merely because it depends on a rejected or canceled patent claim; do not require rewriting into independent form in that circumstance. However, if a new base claim (one not appearing in the patent) has been canceled in a reexamination proceeding, a claim depending thereon should be rejected as indefinite. If a new base claim or an amended patent claim is rejected, an otherwise patentable dependent claim should be objected to and a requirement made to rewrite the dependent claim in independent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status and priority for reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination proceedings must be conducted with 'special dispatch' and are given priority handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 35 U.S.C. 305, all reexamination proceedings (including appeals to the PTAB) are conducted with special dispatch. Cases involved in litigation (reexamination or reissue) have priority over all other cases. Reexaminations not involved in litigation have priority over other cases except those reexaminations or reissues involved in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title-change rules in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on changing the title of the invention during reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally the title need not be changed. If a change is necessary, notify the patent owner early in prosecution as part of an Office Action. If all claims are found patentable and a Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) has been or will be mailed, a change to the title by the examiner may only be done by a formal Examiner’s Amendment. Changing the title by merely initialing the change is not permitted in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner–patent owner discussion practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure allowing examiner to indicate that a discussion with the patent owner’s representative may lead to condition for issuing a NIRC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may, in professional judgment, indicate that a discussion may resolve issues and will contact the patent owner’s representative within about two weeks. Under this practice, the representative can prepare for the discussion. Any resulting amendment may be filed by the patent owner’s attorney/agent or by the examiner as an examiner’s amendment. When extensive amendments are necessary, it is preferable that the patent owner’s attorney/agent file them to provide a better file wrapper record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for preparing the Office action (panel review and signatory requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure after receipt of patent owner response or expiration of response time: examiner prepares for and sets up a panel review conference per MPEP §2271.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may prepare the Office action before or after the conference and revise as needed. If the conference confirms the examiner's preliminary decision to reject and/or allow claims, the Office action shall be issued and signed by the examiner, with two or more conferees initialing the action to indicate their presence. The first ex parte action is intended to establish the issues between examiner and patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing of Office Actions and correspondence address rules
rubrics_metrics.description: How Office actions and copies are mailed and which correspondence address is used for reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination forms are structured to print identifying information and the official correspondence address of record in the patent file (usually the mailing address of the patent owner's legal representative). If no official correspondence address is of record, the Office may treat the patent owner's mailing address as the correspondence address. Where multiple patent owners exist, the Office may treat the mailing address of the first named patent owner as the correspondence address. The Office will not engage in double correspondence with more than one patent owner (37 CFR 1.33(a)). Copies of Office actions are available via Patent Center. All Office actions in a third-party-requested ex parte reexamination will have a copy mailed to the third-party requester using transmittal form PTOL-465. If multiple third-party requesters exist and a requester has not designated a practitioner address, the Office may treat the first named requester’s mailing address as the correspondence address. PTOL-465 is used to track the number of copies and addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for response in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory and typical time periods for responding to Office actions in ex parte reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A shortened statutory period of two months will generally be set for filing a response to an Office action in ex parte reexamination. Extensions of time may be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c). See MPEP §2265 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time practice in ex parte reexamination (37 CFR 1.550(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing requests for extensions of time to take action in ex parte reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request for an extension must specify the requested period and be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g). For third-party-requested ex parte reexamination, a request must be filed on or before the due date and mere filing does not effect an extension; grants require sufficient cause and will not generally be for more than a reasonable time. For patent-owner-requested or Director-ordered ex parte reexamination, a request up to two months from the Office action period must be filed no later than two months after expiration of the original period; requests for more than two months must be filed on or before the original due date, and mere filing will not effect the extension. Replies or other actions must be filed prior to expiration of the granted extension and in no event later than the maximum statutory period. See 37 CFR 1.550(c) and MPEP §2265.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 not permitted in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.136(a) and (b) extensions are not applicable to ex parte reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.136 applies only to 'an applicant' in an application; an ex parte reexamination proceeding does not involve an 'application' or an 'applicant.' Public Law 97-247 and 35 U.S.C. 41 do not make 1.136 applicable. Extensions in ex parte reexamination must be requested pursuant to 37 CFR 1.550(c) with the fee set in 37 CFR 1.17(g). Form paragraph 22.04.01 may be used to notify parties that 1.136 extensions are not permitted and that 1.550(c) governs extension practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for extension of time in ex parte reexamination (37 CFR 1.17(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee per 37 CFR 1.17(g) is required for filing a request for an extension of time in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike the practice under 37 CFR 1.136 where fee amount can determine extension period, the reexamination extension fee is solely for filing the request; the period of extension is not determined by the fee amount. Each request must specify the requested period and be accompanied by the fee. See 37 CFR 1.17(g) and 1.550(c).
